chunks: From him, from ʿAlī, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

I said to him: One who does not know whether he is in four or in two, while he has secured the two? He said: He performs two rakʿahs and four sajdahs while standing, with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, and he recites the tashahhud, and there is nothing upon him. And if he does not know whether he is in three or in four, while he has secured the three, he stands and adds to it one other rakʿah, and there is nothing upon him. And he does not overturn certainty by doubt, nor does he admit doubt into certainty, nor does he mix one of them with the other; rather, he overturns doubt by certainty, and completes upon certainty, so he builds upon it, and he gives no consideration to doubt in any state among the states.

key_terms.الشَّكِّ: doubt concerning the number of rakʿahs
key_terms.الْيَقِينِ: certainty regarding what has definitely been performed
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs to be performed in the prescribed corrective manner
key_terms.سَجَدَاتٍ: prostrations within the rakʿahs of salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَيَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ: he proceeds on the basis of what is certain

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they doubt the number of rakʿahs in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for doubt in the number of rakʿahs in salat (prayer), distinguishing between cases where a lower number has already been secured. It also states the principle that certainty is not nullified by doubt, and that one should build upon what is certain.
